result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: handleNewBooking pushes teamDestinationCalendars into evt.destinationCalendar for COLLECTIVE events, but persistence only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` to the booking. Downstream flows (paypal-webhook, webhook.ts, confirm.handler, bookingReminder, editLocation) all rebuild destinationCalendar as a single-element array from booking.destinationCalendar, so non-organizer hosts' calendars are lost for paid/requires-confirmation collective bookings. This is a verifiable incompleteness/defect in the new multi-destination behavior.

judged_text: Only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected to the booking, so the multi-host destination calendar list computed for collective events is never persisted anywhere in the database. Every flow that rebuilds CalendarEvent from the persisted booking — payment-success webhooks, confirm, reminders — constructs a single-element destinationCalendar from Booking.destinationCalendar, so paid or requires-confirmation collective bookings create calendar events only on the organizer's calendar and never on the other hosts' calendars.

record.issue_text: [BUG] Only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected to the booking, so the multi-host destination calendar list computed for collective events is never persisted anywhere in the database. Every flow that rebuilds CalendarEvent from the persisted booking — payment-success webhooks, confirm, reminders — constructs a single-element destinationCalendar from Booking.destinationCalendar, so paid or requires-confirmation collective bookings create calendar events only on the organizer's calendar and never on the other hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: Diff makes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` an array and, for COLLECTIVE team event types, `handleNewBooking` appends other hosts’ `user.destinationCalendar` values into `evt.destinationCalendar` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking, it still only connects a single destination calendar: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (so only the first/organizer calendar is stored on the Booking). Later flows that reconstruct a `CalendarEvent` from a persisted Booking wrap only `booking.destinationCalendar` (singular) into a one-element array (e.g. bookingReminder, Stripe/PayPal webhooks, confirm, editLocation, deleteCredential, cancel), so the additional collective-host destination calendars are not available and events would only be created/updated for the single persisted calendar.
